text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended narrowly firmer after a listless session. Activity was subdued mainly due to the Ascension Day holiday across Europe and subdued business in New York raws. Front month August ended 80 cents higher at $312.50 per tonne, while October added 20 cents to close at $303.40 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed firmer, buoyed by light speculative and trade buying.

Traders said prices would continue to rise if all the cargoes received from last week's unexpectedly large delivery against May futures can be quickly placed. The physical delivery totalled a hefty 339,950 tonnes, which included 260,000 tonnes of Paranagua raws from one of the largest Brazilian producers. The balance came from north Brazil and three Central American nations.

The heavy delivery with its suggestions of abundant supply produced an initial slump in New York but prices rebounded slightly as it emerged that at least some of the sugar could be early new crop deliveries.

The appearance of new crop south Brazilian sugars against the May contract now means July will see more cargoes delivered when it expires on June 30. Traders said Thai sugar is unlikely to be seen unless futures prices are higher. July ended 8 points higher at 10.84 cents/lb, while October added 5 points to close at 10.69 cents/lb.

INDIA - Sugar production in March 1997 reached 2.717 million tonnes, raw value, 6 per cent less than was produced the same month the previous year. That brought total production since the beginning of 1996/97 (October/September) up to 11.663 million tonnes which compares to 12.807 million tonnes produced the same period in 1995/96 and 12.574 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Production in October/March 1996/97 points to a seasonally adjusted total for the crop year of 14.8 million tonnes which compares to 17.9 million tonnes produced in 1995/96 and 15.9 million tonnes in 1994/95.

RUSSIA - Sugar beet sowings are still behind those of last year. As of May 5 a total of 517,000 ha had been sown which compares to 527,000 ha the same date last year. The total area sown this year is expected to reach 1.080 million ha, slightly up from last year's figure of 1.071 million ha.

DENMARK - Temperatures in the week ended May 5 were just about average most of the time. Cumulative rainfall from April 1 onwards ranged between 29 and 58 mm against an average of 43-45 mm. Germination is still satisfactory given sufficient soil moisture. The overall crop outlook is normal.

The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said it had scrapped tenders invited in April from international suppliers for the import of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar, with shipments to reach Karachi in June and July. A TCP official said fresh tenders would be invited within the next few days. Suppliers would be asked to ship 25,000 tonnes of sugar to Karachi by June 20 and the remaining 25,000 tonnes by July 10.

Pakistan has already imported 484,835 tonnes of sugar worth $185 million during the July/March 1996/97 period. Sugar production up to April 15 reached 2.32 million tonnes, white value, compared to 2.43 million tonnes the same time a year ago. Mills aim to produce 2.4 million tonnes in 1996/97 (October/September) compared to 2.47 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 3.0 million tonnes in 1994/95.

The European Union awarded 20,950 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.085 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on May 7. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to May 7 reached 1,926,000 tonnes, which compares to 2,056,448 tonnes last year.
